message.content: {"summary":"You have written a clearly structured report that reaches a well-reasoned Not Ship conclusion. Your use of the EACE code and the NHS and Volkswagen cases strengthens the case against shipping. To reach the next level, you need more evidence and depth for the pro-shipping case, more accurate sourcing, more measured claims, and recommendations addressed to a wider range of stakeholders.","next_steps":["Check that each citation supports the exact claim it is attached to. The CNBC source does not back your Apple-versus-Samsung and Google claim, and the NHS case should not be presented as directly equivalent to defective server hardware without qualification.","Distinguish physical-harm defects from data-loss defects and tailor your analysis to each, rather than treating all defects as potential harm. Then give separate recommendations for the health department, the chip contractor and your company's management.","Complete and correct your reference list so every entry has author, date, title and URL, and check author attributions. Also soften absolute claims, such as the 'difference between life and death' statement, unless your evidence supports them."],"criteria":{"C1":"You identify several ethical issues, including the trade-off between product quality and business success, harm to end-users, and professional responsibility. You also outline the organisational context and name the key stakeholders. This is a very good response. To reach excellent, link each issue more specifically to engineering design decisions and explain each stakeholder's interests, such as the health department's reliance on the servers, rather than only naming them.","C2":"Your argument against shipping is well developed, and the EACE code and Volkswagen example give it real depth. The case for shipping is thinner and some points are unsupported. The claim that shipping defective units would fund quality improvements is internally inconsistent and needs critical evaluation. Your recommendations focus mainly on Rachel and her company; extend them to the health department and the chip contractor to reach excellent.","C3":"Your report follows a logical sequence from arguments to a clear conclusion, and the Not Ship conclusion follows from the discussion. Some links are weak, particularly the speed-improvement point for shipping. Strengthen the argument by testing the pro-shipping case more seriously and showing how your conclusion addresses all stakeholders. This would make your reasoning more compelling and systematic.","C4":"You use four references, a relevant EACE code and two external cases, which gives your report a solid research base. However, the Apple claim rests on a source that does not support it, and the pro-shipping arguments lack evidence. Adding quantitative or further qualitative evidence, and making sure each source matches its claim, would move your research from moderate towards in-depth and balanced.","C5":"Your report includes the required sections (abstract, introduction, body, conclusion and references), and the writing is generally readable. Correct the language errors: add the missing space in 'ofprofessional', repair the broken sentence in your discussion ('could very well be the difference'), and fix 'Actin'. Complete reference entries: [3] lacks an author and URL, and the author attribution for [4] is incorrect. Adding a figure or table would also help support your discussion."}}
